relations.subject: Leonard William King
relations.evidence: studied King’s College, Cambridge, beginning with theology, but soon Egyptology and Assyriology (B.A. 1891, M.A. 1895, LL.D. 1914).

relations.subject: Leonard William King
relations.role: Assistant Keeper of Egyptian and Assyrian Antiquities
relations.evidence: From 1892 in British Museum, working under Wallis Budge, from 1913 Assistant Keeper of Egyptian and Assyrian Antiquities.

relations.subject: Leonard William King
relations.evidence: In 1910-15 also Lecturer and 1915-19 Professor of Assyrian and Babylonian Archaeology at King’s College, University of London.

relations.subject: Leonard William King
relations.role: Professor of Assyrian and Babylonian Archaeology
relations.evidence: 1915-19 Professor of Assyrian and Babylonian Archaeology at King’s College, University of London.

relations.subject: Leonard William King
relations.evidence: In 1904 —> R. C. Thompson became his Assistant and together they visited Behistun and made copies of the trilingual inscriptions.
